name: 2-ID-E X-ray Fluorescence Microprobe

techniques.name: micro X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy
ptychography
variants: post-APS-U capability per 2022 endstation design paper

techniques.name: micro small-angle X-ray scattering
variants: post-APS-U capability per 2022 endstation design paper

measurables: elemental composition maps at sub-micron scale
quantitative elemental content of single cells (part-per-million detection sensitivity)
3d elemental distribution via xrf tomography and laminography

probe.flux_notes: APS beamline directory (retrieved 2026-08-27): flux 4x10^9 ph/s at 10 keV, Kohzu Si(111) monochromator, energy range 5-20 keV; zone-plate configurations: near-field stack of two zone plates (D=160 um) gives 5x10^8 ph/s at 10 keV, single zone plate (D=320 um) gives ~10x flux. APS-U 2-ID Microprobe endstation (Davis et al. 2022): >10^13 ph/s across 7-20 keV with KB mirror focusing and new combined DCM/DMM monochromator (mono or pink beam).

resolution.spatial_notes: Zone-plate microprobe (beamline directory): focused beam 0.5 um x 0.4 um; near-field stacked zone plates give 0.4 um x 0.3 um probe; single zone plate 0.6 um x 0.4 um at ~10x flux. APS-U 2-ID Microprobe endstation design (Davis et al. 2022, installed in station 2-ID-E): JTEC Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors, achromatic over 7-20 keV, 50 nm spot with asymmetric focusing, 10 um depth of focus, 50 mm working distance.
resolution.energy_notes: Directory lists monochromator energy resolution dE/E = 1.4x10^-4 (Kohzu Si(111)).

sample_constraints.size_notes: Optimized for many-micrometer-thick specimens (XSD-MIC 2-ID-E page). APS-U Microprobe endstation accommodates samples up to 10 x 10 mm at 50 mm working distance; sample holder payload up to 2 kg; XYZ scan travel >=10 mm, fly-scanning at >=25 mm/s with unlimited rotation for tomography (Davis et al. 2022).

sample_environments: environmental specimen chamber optimized for bio-medical and environmental specimens, with kinematic specimen mounting correlated to a Leica DMXRE epi-fluorescence microscope (beamline directory)
sample heating and cooling, including a cryo-cooled 2D sample holder (APS-U endstation design)
detectors: Hitachi (SII) Vortex ME4 4-element silicon drift detector for XRF and spectroscopy
Dectris Eiger2-500K photon-counting area detector for ptychography, laminography and micro-SAXS (APS-U endstation, 700-2000 mm from sample with He flight tube)

data_products.type: 2d quantitative elemental maps with full XRF spectrum per pixel, fitted with APS MAPS / XRF-Maps software

access.proposal_system: APS user proposal system (APS User Portal)

contacts.name: Olga Antipova
contacts.role: beamline contact, 2D/3D XFM and XRF laminography

contacts.name: Barry Lai
contacts.role: beamline contact, 2D/3D XFM; physicist, X-ray Science Division Microscopy group

demonstrated_applications: quantitative zinc mapping in single mouse oocytes/eggs revealing ~8000 zinc-loaded vesicles behind fertilization-induced 'zinc sparks' (Que et al., Nature Chemistry 2015; XFM at APS 2-ID-E and 21-ID-D)
quantification of trace elements (Si, Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn) in individual aquatic protist and plankton cells, 3 to >50 um, for ocean biogeochemistry (Twining et al., Analytical Chemistry 2003)
elemental mapping of trace metals in hepatocellular carcinoma research-model tissues with Vortex ME4 SDD and MAPS peak deconvolution (Frontiers in Public Health 2021)
xrf tomography of composite samples at sub-micron resolution (Microscopy and Microanalysis conference paper)

post-APS-U target applications stated in endstation paper: 3D microelectronics defect metrology, photovoltaic materials, aerosol particles, exogenous and endogenous metal distribution in cells and tissues (Davis et al. 2022)

name: 13-ID-E GSECARS X-ray Microprobe

techniques.name: micro X-ray fluorescence mapping
variants: continuous (fly-scan) mapping with pixel times as low as 5-10 ms

techniques.name: micro X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
variants: high energy resolution fluorescence detection (HERFD) via multi-crystal analyzer spectrometer

techniques.name: micro X-ray diffraction
variants: near-real-time micro-XRD synchronous with micro-XRF mapping

techniques.name: X-ray fluorescence computed microtomography
variants: element-specific fluorescence tomography at micrometer resolution

measurables: trace element distribution in geological/environmental samples
elemental composition (elements with emission energies ~2-28 keV; ppm typical, ppb possible for some samples)
element speciation and oxidation state (micro-XANES, e.g. S, Fe, As K-edges)
mineral phase identification and spatial distribution of crystalline phases (micro-XRD)
3d element-specific internal distribution in small intact specimens (fluorescence microtomography)

probe.flux_notes: 6 x 10^12 photons/sec @ 10 keV with Si(111); 1 x 10^12 photons/sec @ 10 keV with Si(311); 2.1 m, 36 mm period undulator in a canted straight section; cryo-cooled double-crystal monochromator with Si(111) and Si(311) crystal sets

resolution.spatial_notes: New KB mirrors achieve focused spot sizes <500 nm in both vertical and horizontal (GSECARS news item, Sept 23, 2025); typical operating focus 1.5 x 2 um (V x H) via 200-mm Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors; micro-XRD spatial resolution <1 um
resolution.energy_notes: Monochromator energy resolution dE/E = 1.3 x 10^-4 with Si(111), 3 x 10^-5 with Si(311); HERFD available via crystal analyzer spectrometer (up to 3 analyzers, 1-m Rowland circle)

states: small intact specimens (e.g. seeds, roots) for fluorescence tomography
sample_constraints.size_notes: Polished thin sections (e.g. 35-50 um thickness) commonly used for coupled micro-XRF/micro-XRD (published use, Miller et al. 2022); unfocused beam available; offline sample coordinate system available for pre-registration of samples
special_requirements: measurements typically at ambient conditions in air; helium-filled environment available for low-Z / redox-sensitive work

sample_environments: helium-filled environment for redox-sensitive samples and low-energy edges
detectors: Canberra SXD-7 7-element silicon drift detector (SDD) with Xspress3 electronics
multi-crystal analyzer spectrometer (up to 3 analyzers in 1-m Rowland circle geometry)
Vortex-ME4 4-element silicon drift detector (used in published XRF microtomography work)

access.mechanism: APS general user proposal; rapid access proposals accepted for Sector 13 beamlines (from 2025-2 cycle per SEES)

demonstrated_applications: arsenic speciation and mobility in mining-impacted sub-Arctic lake sediments via coupled micro-XRF mapping and micro-XRD on 35-50 um polished thin sections (Miller et al. 2022, PMC8850223)
Mn and Fe localization in Arabidopsis seeds by X-ray fluorescence computed microtomography at ~1 x 2 um resolution, 11 keV (Chu et al. 2017, PMC5591227)
sulfur and iron K-edge micro-XANES of volcanic melt inclusions and matrix glasses to constrain magma redox (PMC12537948; PMC8044198)
trace metal partitioning in soils, wetlands, plant leaves and roots, rock sections, volcanic magmas, micro-meteorites and lunar samples, and cultural artifacts (GSECARS science program page)

provenance.notes: Primary source: energy range 2.4-28 keV, flux, monochromator dE/E, KB mirror focus 0.5x0.5 um (new) and typical 1.5x2 um, techniques (uXAFS, uXRF fly-mapping 5-10 ms pixels, uXRD <1 um, fCMT), detectors, sample environments, ppm typical/ppb possible detection, contacts.
Measurables and application domains: soils, wetlands, plant leaves/roots, rock sections, volcanic magmas, micro-meteorites, lunar samples, cultural artifacts.
Data products/software (Larch; GSE MapViewer, XAS Viewer; Nextcloud transfer) and access route (APS general user proposal).
GSECARS news item dated September 23, 2025: 13-ID-E new mirrors achieve <500 nm focus — post-APS-U performance and evidence of active operation; basis for resolution.spatial_m.

Post-APS-U restart status (as of May 16, 2025): GSECARS commissioning began July 26, 2024; SEES beamlines returned to full user operations for 2025-2/2025-3 cycles; rapid access from 2025-2. Status 'operational' rests on this plus the Sept 2025 mirror news.

CMS Workshop Lectures Vol. 21: confirms coupled uXRD/uXRF/uXAFS mapping and canted-undulator source, 2.4-28 keV (via snippets).
Miller et al. 2022: coupled micro-XRF/micro-XRD at 13-ID-E on 35-50 um thin sections; basis for thin-section constraint.
Chu et al. 2017: SXRF computed microtomography of Arabidopsis seeds at 13-ID-E; ~1x2 um at 11 keV, Vortex-ME4.
S/Fe K-edge XANES of melt inclusions at 13-ID-E (via snippet).
Sulfur oxidation states in mineral inclusions at the GSECARS microprobe (via snippet).

name: Hard X-ray Micro-tomography Beamline 2-BM

techniques.name: phase-contrast imaging
variants: fast 2D phase-contrast radiography of dynamic phenomena

techniques.name: fast / dynamic tomography
variants: real-time GPU reconstruction with on-demand capture and 3D zoom (TomoStream)

techniques.name: X-ray laminography
variants: high-resolution imaging of large slab-shaped samples

techniques.name: high-throughput tomography
variants: automated near video-rate acquisition, hundreds of specimens per day

measurables: pore structure and pore-scale phase change in porous media

probe.flux_notes: Multilayer monochromator (1% bandpass), 8-45 keV; filtered white/pink beam also available. Pre-APS-U: critical energy 19.5 keV, flux ~1.12e13 ph/s/0.1%BW x mrad, beam 50 mm x ~3 mm at 25 m (tomopedia). Post APS-U: BM source fan from B:M4/B:M3 dipoles plus B:Q8 reverse bend of the 6 GeV, 200 mA MBA ring, 5.4 mrad extraction fan (docs2bm); optics are a Y3-30 mirror plus double multilayer monochromator (DMM).

resolution.spatial_notes: Detector pixel sizes 0.32-9 um with 1x/2x/5x/10x/20x lenses (tomopedia); micrometre-scale resolution for fast tomography; ~micrometre resolution demonstrated for whole-mouse-brain laminography (arXiv:2401.11101).
resolution.temporal_notes: Fast tomography with sub-second 3D time resolution. PCO.dimax: 2000 fps at full 2000x2000 frame. Streaming pipeline sustains ~1500-2000 projections/s (16-bit, 1024x1024), >3 GB/s with real-time reconstruction (Nikitin et al. 2022). Fast 2D phase-contrast imaging of dynamics up to 0.1 m/s over 20 x 2 mm^2 field of view (docs2bm).

states: porous media with fluids (in environmental cells)
sample_constraints.size_notes: Parallel-beam geometry; beam 50 mm x ~3 mm at 25 m (pre-APS-U); 20 x 2 mm^2 FOV for fast 2D phase contrast; laminography extends to slab-shaped samples beyond the standard FOV (whole mouse brain in 4 sequential slabs). Kinematic sample mounting (Thorlabs KBT25/KBB25/KBT25T).

sample_environments: induction furnace up to 1000 C in air (water-cooled, Eurotherm controller)
induction furnace up to 1500 C in air (THM 200 heater, Eurotherm controller)
custom in-situ load cell, 600 N capacity
high-pressure fluid delivery: Teledyne ISCO 65D syringe pump up to 20,000 psi
Teledyne ISCO 1000D and Vindum VP-12K pumps up to 12,000 psi at 120 C
environmental cell for gas hydrate / ice formation studies (demonstrated at 7 C, methane)
detectors: FLIR Grasshopper3 9.1 MP (9 fps) / 5.0 MP (75 fps) / 2.3 MP (163 fps)
Teledyne FLIR Oryx 5.0 MP Mono 10GigE (2448x2048, 3.45 um pixels; streaming system)
Optique Peter / MCTOptics detector system with Mitutoyo long-working-distance objectives (1.1x/5x/10x with 100/50/25 um scintillators)

data_products.format: HDF5 (DXfile / Data Exchange schema, written by tomoScan)

data_products.type: real-time streamed slice reconstructions with on-demand HDF5 capture (TomoStream)

typical_experiment_duration: Individual scans down to seconds-minutes; high-throughput mode images hundreds of specimens per day at 2-3 minutes per sample (De Carlo et al. 2006); continuous in-situ campaigns of ~20 hours demonstrated (gas hydrate study).

access.proposal_system: APS User Office / APS user portal
access.cost_model: no-cost for publishable research under DOE user facility policy; proprietary rates apply (standard APS model)

demonstrated_applications: in-situ ice and methane gas hydrate formation in porous samples imaged with real-time streaming tomography over ~20 h (Nikitin et al., J. Synchrotron Rad. 29, 816-828, 2022)
laminography of a whole osmium-stained mouse brain imaged as 4 sequential slabs at micrometre resolution, ~12 TB raw data (Nikitin et al., J. Synchrotron Rad. 31, 2024)
near video-rate high-throughput micro-tomography of hundreds of specimens per day (De Carlo et al., Proc. SPIE 6318, 2006)
fast 2D phase-contrast imaging of dynamic phenomena up to 0.1 m/s over 20 x 2 mm^2 field of view (2-BM docs)
in-situ high-temperature (furnace) and mechanical-loading (600 N load cell) tomography experiments (2-BM docs)

provenance.notes: Energy range 8-45 keV (multilayer, 1% bandpass) + filtered white beam; critical energy 19.5 keV; flux; beam size; camera list; scintillators; lenses 1x-20x; pixel sizes 0.32-9 um; sub-second 3D time resolution; in-situ cells; proposals via APS User Office.
Dedicated microtomography beamline; 20 x 2 mm^2 fast 2D phase-contrast FOV, dynamics to 0.1 m/s.
Sample environments: furnaces to 1000/1500 C, 600 N load cell, Oxford 800 Cryojet, ISCO 65D (20,000 psi), ISCO 1000D and Vindum VP-12K (12,000 psi at 120 C); kinematic mounting.
APS-U source description: 6 GeV, 200 mA MBA ring; B:M4/B:M3 + B:Q8 source fan; 5.4 mrad extraction.

Nikitin et al. 2022 streaming-tomography instrument paper: Oryx camera, Mitutoyo objectives with 100/50/25 um scintillators, >3 GB/s processing on Tesla A100, methane gas-hydrate demonstration at 7 C over ~20 h, on-demand HDF5 capture.
Laminography at 2-BM: micrometre resolution on slab samples; whole mouse brain, 4 slabs, ~12 TB. Published: J. Synchrotron Rad. 31 (2024), doi:10.1107/S1600577524002923.
Current post-APS-U component inventory from GitHub raw: 2-BM-A/B stations, Y3-30 mirror, DMM, MCTOptics + Optique Peter detector; beamline layout drawing dated 05/27/26.
Current user manual: tomocupy/tomopy reconstruction, .h5 raw data, Globus + APS Data Management distribution.

Status evidence: official 2-BM docs actively maintained (latest commits 2026-08-23) with live post-APS-U user manual and 05/2026 layout drawing, indicating user operation after the APS-U restart. aps.anl.gov directory not fetchable (Cloudflare 403); no outage notice found in any source.
De Carlo et al. 2006: near video-rate acquisition, hundreds of specimens/day, 2-3 min per sample (abstract via ADS mirror).
APS GUP call for 2025-2 (via search results): supports access mechanism and post-upgrade user operations in 2025.
